sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129,025 million in FY2017 to $303,154 million in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The shape is a steady compounding line with two step-ups: revenue growth of 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022 against 9.2% in FY2020 [D189][D238][D140].
FY2021's jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase, with e-commerce comparable sales up 44% and gasoline prices adding 100 basis points to net sales [P54][P55].
FY2022 followed on a 14% comparable sales increase, with the strongest growth in gasoline, business centers and travel, and sales still lifted by inflation [P42].
The US segment supplied most of the growth, contributing 6.2pp of FY2025's 8.2% and 7.2pp of FY2026's 10.1% revenue increase [D669][D385][D672][D434].
FY2026's $27,335 million net sales increase was primarily a comparable sales gain of $22,457 million, or 8%, on 5% higher average ticket and 3% higher frequency [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of FY2026 revenue but contributed only 2.6pp of growth, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Operating income grew 12.3% a year against revenue's 10.0%, and operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026 [F204][F203][D458].
Diluted EPS compounded at 14.6% against net income's 14.7%, with the diluted share count essentially flat at 444.4 million [F207][F205][X100].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, its window high, against a 3.4% median and a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat at 87.2% of revenue [D447][D460][D459][D413].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.9pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap of 0.9pp [F52][F32][D448].
Operating cash flow of $15,817 million was 1.71x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $9,382 million was 1.02x net income, above the 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 operating cash increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% against a 2.8% median, with capex at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [D418][D698][D417][D423].
Investing outflow rose to $6,378 million from $5,311 million, primarily capital expenditures [F112][F111][P5].
Net cash reached $15,139 million, or 5.0% of revenue, in FY2026, up from $9,496 million in FY2025 [D427][D428][D378].
That net cash position ranked at the 100th percentile of six retail peers against a -4.4% median, and the current ratio was 1.06x versus a 1.02x median [D715][D716][F182][D704].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3,306 million absorbed 35.2% of free cash flow, with $848 million of repurchases under the January 2023 program [D429][D430][X110][P3].
Long-term debt fell 31.5% to $3,914 million while the diluted share count slipped 0.1% [D445][F192][D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin of 3.0% also ranks 17th against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].
The thin-margin model is structural rather than deteriorating, since the margin is at its window high, but it leaves little cushion if merchandise costs or wages outrun sales.
Free cash flow conversion of 1.02x net income ranked at the 67th percentile against a 0.83x median, and capex has risen to 2.41x D&A from 1.83x in FY2017 [D422][D717][D718][D423][D11].
Rising capital intensity is the item to watch: if capex keeps outpacing depreciation, the free cash flow that funds buybacks and dividends narrows.
Whether FY2027 operating margin holds at the FY2026 high of 3.9% or slips toward the 3.4% median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D692].
Whether free cash flow per dollar of net income stays above the 0.99x median or falls back toward the 0.60x FY2022 low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D701][D699].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue holds above the FY2026 5.0% or reverses toward the FY2024 2.1%, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D428][D330].
